title: TCS Posts Strong Q1 as AI Revenue Hits $2.6 Billion Run Rate, Plans 8,900 AI Engineers and Acquisition Push
excerpt: India's largest IT exporter beat revenue estimates on banking demand and accelerating AI deployments, though order book dipped and AI revenue growth slowed from the prior quarter.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • TCS reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 72,275 crore, up 14% year-on-year.
  • AI services revenue reached $2.6 billion, growing 13% quarter-on-quarter.
  • The company plans to hire 8,900 AI engineers and pursue acquisitions.
  • TCS added 9,300 employees, marking its fastest hiring pace in over three years.

  • TCS reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs 72,275 crore ($7.58 billion), up 14% year-on-year, beating analyst estimates
  • Annualized AI services revenue crossed $2.6 billion, up from $2.3 billion the prior quarter, though growth slowed to 13% from 28%
  • The company plans to deploy up to 8,900 AI engineers and is actively seeking AI-related acquisitions
  • TCS added 9,300 employees in the quarter — its fastest hiring pace in over three years

Tata Consultancy Services, India's largest software services exporter, delivered a stronger-than-expected first quarter powered by banking demand and rising artificial intelligence revenue, but a slowing AI growth rate and a shrinking order book temper the optimism about a full-blown sector recovery.

The Numbers

TCS reported revenue of Rs 72,275 crore ($7.58 billion) for the quarter ended June 2026, up 14% year-on-year and 2.7% in constant-currency terms. Net profit rose 4.6% to Rs 13,349 crore. The company's board declared an interim dividend of Rs 12 per share.

The order book stood at $9.5 billion, including what the company called "a marquee AI-led transformation deal with SKF." That figure is down from $12 billion in the March quarter, though management framed it as reflecting lumpy deal timing rather than weakening demand.

AI: The Growth Engine

Annualized AI services revenue crossed $2.6 billion, driven by faster deployments across industries. The metric, which TCS began disclosing in December, rose 13% quarter-on-quarter — a noticeable deceleration from the 28% growth logged in the prior three months.

"What you need is a deep knowledge of the customer environment to make it work. That is where we differentiate ourselves. This has nothing to do with cost arbitrage."

— K Krithivasan, CEO, Tata Consultancy Services

CEO K Krithivasan dismissed concerns that AI would disrupt the outsourcing model, arguing that companies still need partners like TCS to integrate and deploy AI systems across complex enterprise environments. He said he targets 25% quarter-on-quarter AI revenue growth over the long term but does not expect a linear trajectory.

Hiring Surge and Acquisition Plans

TCS added approximately 9,300 employees during the quarter — its fastest hiring pace in more than three years. The company disclosed plans to deploy up to 8,900 AI deployment engineers and said it spends about $1 billion annually on talent development.

CFO Samir Seksaria told Reuters the company is also actively looking at AI-related acquisitions. "We are looking at where we can find things which will help us enable or enhance our strategic positioning," he said.

What It Means for NRI Investors and Tech Workers

TCS shares rose as much as 4.1% following the results, lifting the broader IT index by 1.8%. Analysts at Centrum Broking noted that investors are pricing in positive growth expectations for coming quarters, led by AI adoption.

For the roughly 600,000 TCS employees worldwide — many of whom work in the United States on H-1B visas — the results suggest relative job security at a time when the broader tech sector faces uncertainty. Krithivasan signaled a second-quarter recovery in manufacturing and life sciences demand, two segments that had been sluggish.

However, a Reuters Breakingviews analysis cautioned that TCS's AI revenue metric is "blurry" and difficult to compare across the industry, noting that the deceleration in growth warrants scrutiny even as headline numbers beat expectations.
